newsitem.title: MEXICO: Two dead, not 14, in Mexico train crash - Red Cross.
newsitem.headline: Two dead, not 14, in Mexico train crash - Red Cross.

text.p: Two railroad workers died when a locomotive derailed just outside Mexico City on Wednesday, the Mexican Red Cross and Mexican National Railroad said.

A Red Cross radio operator earlier reported that 14 people had died in a passenger train accident, but Red Cross radio operator Carlos Alquicira corrected his colleague, telliing Reuters, "That's totally wrong. Only two cadavers were recovered from the scene."

The Mexican National Railroad reported that two workers died and three were injured when the train derailed while transporting equipment. It was not a passenger train, as the Red Cross reported earlier.

Engineer Gonzalo Torres Diego and his assistant Daniel Monroy Tavares were killed, the national railroad company said. A conductor and two other rail workers were injured, the rail company said in a statement.
"The causes of the accident are being investigated," the statement said.
Alquicira, the Red Cross radio operator, said it was unclear how the erroneous information had been reported.
